seo.title: Hear Your Baby's Heartbeat at Home
seo.description: Listen to your baby's real heartbeat at home with just your iPhone and headphones — no extra device. Record it, keep it, share it. From around week 22.
cookie.text: We use cookies to enhance your experience and analyze site traffic.
hero.title:
Hear your baby's heartbeat.
*No device. Just your phone.*
hero.sub: Snuggly reveals the real sound of your baby's heart in the womb — gently, at home, whenever you want to listen.
hero.note: Works best with AirPods or any headphones
phone.alt: Sharing a heartbeat recording in the Snuggly app
promise.quote: The room goes quiet, you press play, and there it is — *a fast little flutter that's been with you all along.* Suddenly the bump is a someone.
promise.sig: A moment most parents never get to hear until the next ultrasound. Snuggly brings it home.
how.title: Three quiet steps to your first listen
how.lede: No setup, no accessories. If you have your phone and a pair of headphones, you're ready.
how.step1.title: Open the app
how.step1.body: Pop your headphones in, turn the volume up, and find a calm, quiet spot to settle into.
how.step2.title: Place it on your belly
how.step2.body: Rest the phone flat against your bump, low and slightly to one side, and move slowly to find the spot.
how.step3.title: Listen & record
how.step3.body: When the heartbeat comes through, tap record to keep the moment as a keepsake forever.
science.title:
We don't fake the sound.
*We reveal it.*
science.lede: Snuggly is built on psychoacoustics research. The algorithm amplifies the heartbeat's key frequencies and gently filters out background noise — so the sound that reaches you is the one that was already there.
science.point1: **Nothing is synthesized.** No generated sounds, no stand-in heartbeats — only what your phone's microphone actually picks up.
science.point2: **Noise out, heartbeat in.** Signal processing separates the rhythmic pulse from the rustle of everyday sound around it.
science.point3: **Tuned for tiny sounds.** The key frequencies of a fetal heartbeat are lifted just enough to come through clearly in your headphones.
science.vizCaption: Background noise filtered out — the real pulse amplified.
features.title: Made for the moments you'll want to keep
features.lede: From your very first listen to the keepsakes you'll share with family — gentle features for a tender time.
features.live.title: Listen live
features.live.body: Place your phone on your belly and hear the heartbeat in real time through your headphones.
features.record.title: Record keepsakes
features.record.body: Save the moments that catch you off guard and keep them in a library you can return to anytime.
features.reminders.title: Weekly reminders
features.reminders.body: A gentle nudge each week — *“Time to make a memory”* — so the bump-period moments don't slip by.
features.share.title: Share as beautiful videos
features.share.body: Turn a recording into something worth posting, with three built-in templates designed for family and socials.
cta.title: Your baby is already saying hello.
cta.body: Download Snuggly and listen for the first time tonight.
tips.title: A few small things make a big difference
tips.lede: Fetal heartbeats are quiet sounds. A calm room and these gentle adjustments help Snuggly find them.
tips.1.title: Use headphones
tips.1.body: AirPods or any Bluetooth headphones are strongly recommended — phone speakers won't do the sound justice.
tips.2.title: Remove your phone case
tips.2.body: A bare phone sits flush against your belly, so nothing muffles the microphone.
tips.3.title: Turn the volume up
tips.3.body: Set your volume near the max before you start, then settle into a quiet room.
tips.4.title: Tilt slightly
tips.4.body: A small tilt of the phone often brings the heartbeat into focus — experiment gently.
tips.5.title: Move slowly
tips.5.body: Glide the phone across your bump a little at a time, pausing to listen as you go.
faq.title: Questions, gently answered
faq.a1: No. Snuggly is made for connection and keepsakes, not diagnosis. It isn't a medical device and shouldn't be used to monitor your baby's health. For anything medical, always talk to your healthcare provider.
faq.q2: From which week does it work?
faq.a2: We usually recommend starting around week 22, when your baby's heartbeat is more likely to be picked up clearly. Earlier than that, it can be harder to hear anything — and that's completely normal. Every pregnancy and body is different, so your experience may vary week to week.
faq.a3: Not yet — Snuggly is currently an iPhone app, tuned specifically for Apple's microphones and audio hardware. Android support isn't available today.
faq.a4: Snuggly works on recent iPhones running an up-to-date version of iOS. For the best results, pair it with AirPods or any Bluetooth headphones.
faq.q5: Does it use the internet or store recordings in the cloud?
faq.a5: Listening and recording happen right on your phone. Your keepsakes stay with you on your device unless you choose to share them — they aren't uploaded to the cloud for you.
disclaimer.p1: Snuggly is a keepsake app for hearing and recording your baby's heartbeat. **It is not a medical device and is not intended for diagnostic or monitoring use.**
disclaimer.p2: Snuggly should never replace prenatal care or professional medical advice. If you have any concerns about your pregnancy or your baby's wellbeing, please contact your doctor, midwife, or healthcare provider.
footer.tagline: Tiny heartbeat, lifetime memory. Made with care for expecting parents.
